raw.etymology_text:
From Middle High German vür, from Old High German furi, from Proto-West Germanic *furi, from Proto-Germanic *furi.
Historically also used interchangeably with the related vor in its locational sense. In the 18th century, grammarians established a clearer split with für being prescribed for its chief modern senses of "for (the benefit of), in exchange for".
